subtitle: How the Fourth Guru Drew a City Around a Pool of Nectar

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a dusty plain with a shimmering unfinished pool at its heart
panels.action: Guru Ram Das stands calm at the edge of a half-dug basin on the Punjab plain, robed simply, as workers toil in the background and a faint vision of a future city shimmers behind him.

dialogue.text: In the age of the fourth Guru, a dusty hollow became Ramdaspur, and a pool of water became the beating heart of Amritsar.

i18n.hi: चौथे गुरु के समय, एक सूखी खाई रामदासपुर बनी, और एक जलकुंड अमृतसर का धड़कता दिल।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Guru Ram Das in serene contemplation, background fading into soft light
panels.action: Guru Ram Das sits cross-legged on a simple woven mat, eyes half-closed in meditation, his face lined with quiet resolve, as faint outlines of villages and caravans float like shadows behind him.

dialogue.text: Born Jetha in 1534, orphaned young, he grew through sewa and song until, in 1574, the mantle of Guru rested upon his shoulders.

i18n.hi: १५३४ में जेठा के रूप में जन्म, बचपन में अनाथ; सेवा और कीर्तन में पले, १५७४ में गुरुगद्दी उनके सिर पर आई।

panels.shot: wide shot of Goindwal with pilgrims on the Baoli steps, Guru Ram Das helping quietly among them
panels.action: In the bustling pilgrimage town of Goindwal, Guru Ram Das bends to support an old pilgrim on the stone steps of the Baoli, while traders and travelers crowd around the sacred well.

dialogue.text: Under Guru Amar Das at Goindwal, he learned to weave devotion with organization, turning the flow of pilgrims into a school of service and discipline.

i18n.hi: गोइंदवाल में गुरु अमरदास से, उन्होंने भक्ति को प्रबंध के साथ बुनना सीखा, यात्रियों की धारा को सेवा और अनुशासन की पाठशाला बना दिया।

panels.shot: bird's-eye view of countryside between scattered villages, with Guru Ram Das walking along a dusty path
panels.action: Guru Ram Das walks along a narrow path between mustard fields and scattered hamlets, a small group of Sikhs following, while distant villages and shallow ponds dot the horizon.

dialogue.text: The Panjab was a patchwork of villages, tanks and trading tracks, watched by Mughal officers and zamindars, shaken by droughts, taxes and rivalries.

i18n.hi: पंजाब गांवों, तालाबों और व्यापारिक राहों की जाली था; मुगल अफसर और ज़मींदार निगरानी में, सूखे, लगान और दुश्मनियों से हिलता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium wide shot at a low marshy depression near a village, Guru Ram Das observing the land
panels.action: Guru Ram Das stands at the edge of a shallow, marshy depression beside scrub and scattered trees, farmers watching curiously from a nearby hamlet as he studies the shape of the land.

dialogue.text: Near the village of Tung lay a low-lying spot, a natural hollow for water. Later records remember land bought here for seven hundred rupees, a deliberate claim on earth and future.

i18n.hi: तूंग गांव के पास एक नीची जगह थी, पानी की प्राकृतिक खोह। बाद की लिखतें बताती हैं कि यहां सात सौ रुपये देकर ज़मीन खरीदी गई—धरती और आने वाले कल पर जानबूझ कर दावा।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Guru Ram Das addressing a small group of Sikhs under a tree
panels.action: Under the shade of a spreading tree, Guru Ram Das speaks to a circle of seated Sikhs, his hand gesturing towards the distant hollow as they listen with intent faces.

dialogue.text: Where other men built forts, he chose a depression in the earth. He would build around water, not walls; around sewa, not pride.

i18n.hi: जहाँ और लोग किले उठाते थे, उन्होंने धरती की ही धँसी जगह चुनी। वे पानी के चारों ओर बसाएंगे, दीवारों के नहीं; सेवा के चारों ओर, अहंकार के नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of early Ramdaspur, with simple huts, a few tents, and the first lines of the sarovar marked
panels.action: Simple thatched huts and cloth tents cluster on the edge of the chosen hollow as Guru Ram Das walks among them, laying out the lines of the future pool with a staff in his hand.

dialogue.text: So Ramdaspur was seeded: a scatter of dwellings around an empty bowl in the earth, the Guru’s presence the only ornament, the promise of water its only boast.

i18n.hi: यूँ रामदासपुर की नींव रखी गई: धरती की खाली कटोरी के चारों ओर बिखरे घर, गुरु की हाज़िरी ही एकमात्र शान, आने वाले पानी का वादा ही गर्व।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle shot of workers digging, earth flying, Guru Ram Das joining in
panels.action: Men and women heave baskets of soil from the depression as spades bite into earth; Guru Ram Das himself grips a spade, body bent to the task, robes dusted, face glowing with effort.

dialogue.text: Excavation began not with hired armies, but with hands of sewadars. The Guru dug beside them, making labor itself a form of remembrance.

i18n.hi: खुदाई किसी मज़दूर फौज से नहीं, सेवादारों के हाथों से शुरू हुई। गुरु खुद संग कुदाल चलाते, मजदूरी को ही स्मरण बना देते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Guru Ram Das speaking to a gathered sangat of different backgrounds
panels.action: A diverse group of Sikhs—farmers, artisans, traders—sit in a semicircle facing Guru Ram Das, who raises his hand as if dividing ten parts with his fingers.

dialogue.text: Set aside a tenth, and let the Guru's work be your treasure.

i18n.hi: आमदनी का दसवां हिस्सा अलग रखो, गुरु का काम ही तुम्हारा खज़ाना बने।

panels.shot: close-up of hands placing coins, grain, and tools into a shared basket
panels.action: A woven basket fills with coins, grain, and small tools as different hands—rough, jeweled, calloused—place their offerings together while Guru Ram Das watches quietly in the blurred background.

dialogue.text: Dasvandh—one-tenth offered—turned scattered devotion into steady resource, feeding the sarovar, the langar, and the rising streets of Ramdaspur.

i18n.hi: दसवंध—दसवां हिस्सा अर्पित—ने बिखरी भक्ति को निरंतर साधन बनाया, सरोवर, लंगर और उभरती रामदासपुर की गलियों को पोसता रहा।

panels.shot: wide shot of artisans at work in a growing bazaar street, Guru Ram Das walking through
panels.action: A narrow street lined with fresh wooden stalls shows weavers at looms, a smith at his forge, a grocer arranging jars, as Guru Ram Das walks through, nodding to each craftsperson.

dialogue.text: He invited traders and artisans to settle, so that faith and livelihood would breathe together. Pilgrimage would bring commerce; commerce would sustain pilgrimage.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने व्यापारियों और कारीगरों को बसने बुलाया, ताकि रोज़ी और रब्ब दोनों साथ सांस लें। यात्रा से रोज़गार आए, रोज़गार से यात्रा टिके।

panels.shot: medium wide shot of Guru Ram Das meeting a visiting merchant caravan at the outskirts
panels.action: A small caravan of pack animals and carts pauses as a turbaned merchant bows to Guru Ram Das, who welcomes him with open palms, the half-built pool and huts visible behind them.

dialogue.text: Here, let profit and prayer walk the same street.

i18n.hi: यहाँ लाभ और लिबास, दोनों एक ही गली में चलें।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a simple shelter, Guru Ram Das composing, with a student nearby writing
panels.action: Inside a modest shelter, Guru Ram Das sits with eyes lifted, lips moving softly; beside him, a Sikh scribe leans over a leaf of paper, reed pen poised to catch each word.

dialogue.text: As the pool deepened outside, hymns flowed within. Over six hundred shabads, including the Lavan, gave voice to union, discipline and joy.

i18n.hi: बाहर कुंड गहरा होता गया, भीतर कीर्तन बहते रहे। छह सौ से अधिक शब्द, लावਾਂ समेत, एकता, अनुशासन और आनंद की आवाज़ बने।

panels.shot: intimate close-up on Guru Ram Das’s serene face as he recites, candlelight flickering
panels.action: Candlelight flickers across the gentle, intent face of Guru Ram Das as he recites, his hand raised slightly as if tracing invisible circles in the air.

dialogue.text: He sang of four rounds of spiritual journey in the Lavan, not yet a fixed marriage rite, but a path of the soul circling ever closer to the Beloved.

i18n.hi: लावां में उन्होंने रूहानी सफ़र के चार फेरे गाए—अभी विवाह की रीति नहीं, बल्के रूह का प्रियतम के और पास घूमता सफ़र।

panels.shot: wide shot of the nearly completed sarovar filled with water, people bathing and sitting in reflection
panels.action: The broad, stepped pool now brims with clear water; men and women descend to its edge, some bathing, some sitting in silent reflection, while Guru Ram Das stands watching from one corner.

dialogue.text: At last the hollow held water. The sarovar mirrored the sky, and the city began to see itself not in walls and towers, but in shared reflection.

i18n.hi: आखिर गड्ढा पानी से भर गया। सरोवर ने आकाश को आईना दिखाया, और शहर ने खुद को दीवारों- मीनारों में नहीं, साझा प्रतिबिंब में देखना शुरू किया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Guru Ram Das addressing a gathering by the water at sunset
panels.action: At sunset by the glowing water, Guru Ram Das stands before a seated sangat, his silhouette dark against the shimmering pool as they listen in attentive silence.

dialogue.text: This pool is a place of remembrance. Let your pride sink here.

i18n.hi: यह कुंड स्मरण का स्थान है। अपना अहंकार यहीं डुबो दो।

panels.shot: bird's-eye view of Ramdaspur expanding around the sarovar, lanes and houses in a loose grid
panels.action: From above, the sarovar lies at the center while new lanes and brick houses spread around it, smoke rising from courtyards, markets busy, and small processions moving towards the water.

dialogue.text: Ramdaspur grew by the logic of the pool. Streets bent towards it; markets fed those who came; the Guru’s house was not a palace but a center of hearing and giving.

i18n.hi: रामदासपुर ने कुंड की तर्ज़ पर रूप लिया। गलियाँ उसकी ओर मुड़तीं, बाज़ार आने वालों को संभालते, गुरु का घर महल नहीं, सुनने और देने का केंद्र था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Guru Ram Das with his son (kept generic) near the sarovar, pointing to the town
panels.action: Guru Ram Das walks along the edge of the sarovar with a younger Sikh at his side, gesturing out toward the growing town as if entrusting its care to the next generation.

dialogue.text: He would not see every wall raised, nor every shrine rebuilt in later centuries, yet he set the pattern: water, word, and organized sewa as the frame of Sikh life.

i18n.hi: वे हर दीवार का उठना नहीं देख पाए, न आने वाली सदियों के हर थान का बनना; पर ढांचा वे ही दे गए—पानी, शब्द और संगठित सेवा पर खड़ी सिख ज़िंदगी।

panels.shot: long-term time-lapse style wide shot: faint overlays of future Amritsar around the same sarovar site
panels.action: The same sarovar is shown as a constant center while faint ghostly images of later brick embankments, domes, and crowds through the centuries rise and fade around it, Guru Ram Das’s calm figure in the foreground.

dialogue.text: Though the shrine and sarovar would be rebuilt many times, the site endured. From Ramdaspur to Amritsar, the city’s strength lay in a Guru who dug a pool and called all to serve around it.

i18n.hi: मंदिर और सरोवर कई बार बने-बिगड़े, पर स्थल अडिग रहा। रामदासपुर से अमृतसर तक, शहर की ताकत उस गुरु में रही जिसने कुंड खोदा और सबको उसकी परिक्रमा में सेवा को बुलाया।

title_i18n.en: Guru Ram Das Digs the Pool of Nectar
title_i18n.hi: गुरु राम दास: अमृत कुंड की खुदाई

subtitle_i18n.hi: चौथे गुरु ने अमृत कुंड के चारों ओर शहर कैसे बसाया
